facts.P1_fx_receipts: Yes; you may freely own and use foreign currency.
facts.P2_fcy_account: Yes: you may hold foreign-currency deposits at Indonesian banks.
facts.P3_local_gateways: Midtrans accepts individuals with a KTP; Xendit needs a registered company.
facts.L1_registration: Businesses get an NIB online through OSS; individuals register with NIK and NPWP.
facts.L2_tax_id: Your NIK (national ID number) is your tax ID (NPWP).
facts.L3_income_tax_foreign: Worldwide income taxed; 0.5% final tax on turnover up to Rp4.8bn, first Rp500m free.
facts.L4_vat_gst: VAT 11% effective; register only above Rp4.8 billion; listed exported services are 0%.
facts.L5_data_protection: PDP Law 27/2022 applies fully since October 2024; its agency isn't confirmed yet.
facts.L6_consumer_ecommerce: E-commerce rules (PP 80/2019) apply; licence needs for your own website are unclear.
facts.L7_incentives: 0.5% final tax with no time limit, and the first Rp500m a year untaxed.
facts.D1_id_document: KTP-el electronic ID card, carrying your NIK.

watch_out.text: Foreign income counts toward the Rp4.8 billion limit for the 0.5% tax.
Xendit doesn't accept individuals; you'd need a single-person company (PT Perorangan).
